name: Uterine Arteriovenous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Demonstration of abnormal direct arteriovenous shunting within the uterus on Doppler ultrasound, CT angiography, or MRI
Recurrent, profuse, and unexplained uterine bleeding not attributable to other causes
Exclusion of other causes of abnormal uterine bleeding such as retained products of conception, gestational trophoblastic disease, or malignancy
Selective pelvic angiography confirming arteriovenous malformation and feeding vessels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation with imaging evidence of uterine AVM and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis often requires multimodal imaging; angiography is gold standard but invasive

pathognomonic.symptomName: High-velocity turbulent flow on Doppler ultrasound
searchTerms: fast turbulent blood flow on ultrasound
noisy blood flow detected by Doppler

common.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
searchTerms: low red blood cells from ongoing blood loss

common.notes: Palpable on physical exam or imaging

searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells
heart failure with high blood flow
circulatory collapse due to massive hemorrhage

laboratory: Anemia on complete blood count due to chronic blood loss
imaging: Color Doppler ultrasound showing high-velocity, low-resistance flow with multiple serpiginous vascular channels
Pelvic MRI demonstrating flow voids consistent with vascular malformation
Pelvic angiography confirming arteriovenous shunting and feeding vessels
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; typically acquired or idiopathic
other: Histopathology rarely performed; shows abnormal direct connections between arteries and veins without intervening capillaries

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of intrauterine tissue on ultrasound
Positive pregnancy test or recent pregnancy history
No abnormal vascular flow pattern typical of AVM
Lack of high-velocity turbulent flow on Doppler
Usually no severe hemorrhage unless degeneration occurs

redFlags: Sudden onset of profuse vaginal bleeding
High-output cardiac failure symptoms in context of uterine AVM
references: Timor-Tritsch IE, Monteagudo A. Color Doppler ultrasound diagnosis of uterine arteriovenous malformations. J Ultrasound Med. 1997;16(6): 415-420.
Yoon DJ, Jones M, Rock JA, et al. Uterine arteriovenous malformations: a review of the literature. Obstet Gynecol Surv. 2016;71(7): 385-393.
Sharma S, Gupta M, Gupta R, et al. Uterine arteriovenous malformation: diagnosis and management. J Obstet Gynaecol India. 2018;68(3): 204-209.
